passages.text: Thus the egg that first formed, warmed from below by the living creature within, bursts. Then, having taken form, it comes forth, of a kind that Orpheus also describes: “when the hard, very capacious egg was split.” And thus, once he himself—the one who has come forth—has appeared with great power, the mass receives its cohesion and obtains its ordered arrangement. He himself sits as though at the summit of heaven, while, amid secret things, shining all around the boundless age. As for the fertile matter left inside the mass: it lay underneath over a long period, until the heat, naturally seething beneath, separated the substances of all things. For its lowest part first sank downward under its weight like sediment. Because of its heaviness, and because the quantity of the underlying substance was weighty and large, they named it Pluto, declaring him king of Hades and of the dead.

lexical_decisions.chosen: warmed from below by the living creature within
lexical_decisions.rationale: The compound heating verb retains the under/beneath nuance. The living creature is explicitly the agent of the warming; no separate fire source is added.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἔπειτα δὲ μορφωθὲν προέρχεται ὁποῖόν τι καὶ Ὀρφεὺς λέγει
lexical_decisions.chosen: Then, having taken form, it comes forth, of a kind that Orpheus also describes
lexical_decisions.rationale: The subject of the neuter participle and verb is not newly named. It is contextually the inner creature that appears, but the previous egg is also neuter; the main text leaves “it” while the subsequent masculine description represents the emerging figure. ὁποῖόν τι characterizes its kind or form, rather than introducing a newly specified shape.

lexical_decisions.chosen: when the hard, very capacious egg was split
lexical_decisions.rationale: The printed κραναίου is unusual; “hard” is a contextual interpretation associated with the Greek κραναός family’s hard/rugged sense, not a claim that this precise form has been uniquely established as that lemma. “Rugged” is a less interpretive alternative, but less natural for an egg. The Greek is not normalized to κραναοῦ or replaced with an editor’s conjectural epithet. πολυχανδέος denotes capacity to contain much, expressed as “very capacious”; no literal stone material or lost shell noun is supplied.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸ μὲν κύτος τὴν ἁρμονίαν λαμβάνει καὶ τὴν διακόσμησιν ἴσχει
lexical_decisions.chosen: the mass receives its cohesion and obtains its ordered arrangement
lexical_decisions.rationale: κύτος can denote a hollow body, enclosing bulk, or cavity; “mass” refers to the enclosing whole in this cosmogony, not a newly named universe. ἁρμονία is its joining/cohesion; “harmony” is a more literal alternative, and διακόσμησις is its arrangement or ordering.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐν ἀπορρήτοις τὸν ἄπειρον περιλάμπων αἰῶνα
lexical_decisions.chosen: amid secret things, shining all around the boundless age
lexical_decisions.rationale: The masculine participle retains the emerging figure as its subject. ἀπορρήτοις can denote secret or unspeakable things, with “in mysteries” a contextual alternative. αἰών can be an age, duration, or cosmic world-order; the main text keeps “age” and the surrounding illumination without uniquely selecting an eternal duration or a named realm.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἡ δὲ τοῦ κύτους ἔνδοθεν γόνιμος ὑπολειφθεῖσα ὕλη, ὡς ἐν πολλῷ τῷ χρόνῳ ὑποκειμένη ἕως φυσικῶς ὑποζέουσα ἡ θερμότης, τὰς πάντων διέκρινεν οὐσίας.
lexical_decisions.chosen: As for the fertile matter left inside the mass: it lay underneath over a long period, until the heat, naturally seething beneath, separated the substances of all things
lexical_decisions.rationale: The selected nominative ὑποκειμένη can agree with the initial ὕλη. I read that initial noun phrase and the ὡς-plus-participle circumstance as a suspended topic: the matter as lying underneath over a long period. The sentence then shifts to heat as the subject of διέκρινεν inside a temporal ἕως-clause. φυσικῶς qualifies ὑποζέουσα, the nominative participle agreeing with ἡ θερμότης. English resumes the topic with “it lay,” converting the surviving participial description into a finite predicate, rather than claiming that a lost Greek verb has been found. ὡς contributes the circumstance in which the matter is presented; the English topic-and-resumption structure does not claim that ὡς itself literally means “as for.” The Greek remains marked anacoluthon, with no independent finite predicate for the initial matter-topic. This is a proposed contextual analysis, not a regular-syntax proof or uniquely established reading. “Until” preserves ἕως without deletion or emendation. If the independent reviewer finds this verbal resumption unsupported, the candidate remains unresolved.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὃ διὰ τὴν ὁλκότητα καὶ διὰ τὸ ἐμβριθὲς καὶ πολὺ τῆς ὑποκειμένης οὐσίας πλῆθος Πλούτωνα προσηγόρευσαν
lexical_decisions.chosen: Because of its heaviness, and because the quantity of the underlying substance was weighty and large, they named it Pluto
lexical_decisions.rationale: Both expressions of weight are represented: ὁλκότης and ἐμβριθές. πολὺ preserves the great quantity. “Pluto” is the conventional name; the lower substance’s naming as a personal ruler is the author’s own shift and is not harmonized away.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ οὕτω μεγάλῃ δυνάμει αὐτοῦ τοῦ προεληλυθότος φανέντος, τὸ μὲν κύτος τὴν ἁρμονίαν λαμβάνει καὶ τὴν διακόσμησιν ἴσχει
lexical_decisions.chosen: And thus, once he himself—the one who has come forth—has appeared with great power, the mass receives its cohesion and obtains its ordered arrangement
lexical_decisions.rationale: The genitive absolute φανέντος presents the emerging figure’s manifestation as the circumstance accompanying or preceding the mass’s cohesion. μεγάλῃ δυνάμει characterizes that appearance, “with great power,” rather than being directly attached as the means by which the mass receives cohesion. The perfect προεληλυθότος is represented as “who has come forth”; the aorist φανέντος is represented as completed manifestation, “has appeared,” before the historical-present receives/obtains clauses. αὐτοῦ supplies the personal emphasis, “he himself.” A causal understanding of the absolute is also possible, approximately “because he himself, the one who has come forth, has appeared with great power”; it would make the manifestation as a whole causal, not the power alone. The main temporal-circumstantial analysis does not uniquely exclude that alternative.

source_issues.issue: This candidate follows the human-authorized, independently image-checked public-domain Dressel 1853 reading, printed page 160, PDF page 173, associated with O/Ottobonianus 443. The former selected Lagarde reading is preserved here exactly: ὑποκειμένης ἕως φυσικῆς. Dressel’s apparatus also records that genitive reading under C; the nominative/adverb variant is not a recovery of an undisputed original. The source curation changes only the two documented forms, not ἕως. The marked syntax and English verbal resumption are explained in the lexical note; a missing Greek predicate is not restored. Fresh independent source-and-translation review remains mandatory.
